_README: THE REGISTRANT BOUNDARY REGISTER -- every CIK a ticker's filings may come from.
A ticker's price history follows the ECONOMIC entity; its filings follow the LEGAL
registrant. When a company reorganises under a new holding company or re-registers in
another jurisdiction, the registrant's CIK changes and the price history does not.
`Company(ticker)` resolves exactly one CIK -- the one EDGAR's ticker table points at
TODAY -- so everything the predecessor filed becomes invisible with no error, no
exception and no gap signal. The ticker simply arrives with 22 filings where its peers
have 62, and nothing says why.
SEGMENTS, NOT TWO CIKs. `segments` is ordered oldest-first and CONTIGUOUS: the
`valid_from` of each segment equals the `valid_to` of the one before it, the oldest omits
`valid_from` and the newest omits `valid_to`. Chains are real -- PSKY is CBS -> Viacom ->
ViacomCBS -> Paramount Global -> Paramount Skydance -- and a two-CIK schema gives such a
ticker one hop and leaves the rest truncated.
A BOUNDARY IS `< valid_to` AND `>= valid_from`: strictly before / on-or-after. Adjacent
segments are therefore disjoint by construction rather than by de-duplication.
HOW THE SEGMENTS COMBINE IS A PROPERTY OF THE FORM, NOT OF THIS FILE. Event forms (8-K,
13D, 13G, Forms 3/4/5) take the UNION of every segment CIK; consolidating forms (10-K,
10-Q, DEF 14A) take the DATED SPLIT. Both rules are measured, and they are not
reconcilable into one: against APA's 2021-03-01 boundary the predecessor filed 4,291
Form 4s (4 after the boundary) and 140 10-K/10-Qs (15 after). A union of the event stream
gains 4,287 filings and risks 4; a union of the consolidating stream would blend 15
subsidiary 10-K/10-Qs into the parent's accounts -- a fuller-looking history that is
quietly wrong, which is the dangerous direction. See `common/registrant.FORM_POLICY`.
A RENAME IS NOT A CUTOVER AND BELONGS NOWHERE IN THIS FILE. CVS Caremark -> CVS Health
and Facebook -> Meta keep their CIK; an entry for either would walk one CIK twice and
duplicate every filing. `kind` may only be `reorganisation` or `domestication`, and the
loader rejects `kind: rename` BY NAME so the mistake cannot be made quietly. Sharadar
records a name change whether or not the CIK moved, which is exactly why the shell-name
evidence that motivates most entries here also fits a pure rename -- IVZ (AMVESCAP plc ->
Invesco) carries such an action and is NOT in this file, because CIK 914208 filed
continuously from 1994.
⚠ RISK ZONE. The failure mode is QUIET DATA LOSS: a `valid_to` set a year early drops the
predecessor's last four filings and admits nothing in their place, and nothing downstream
can tell that from a company that genuinely filed nothing. A wrong entry cannot raise on
its own, which is why every segment carries `evidence` and why the loader raises on every
malformed entry it CAN detect. Add an entry only with three oracles agreeing; see
`scripts/detect_registrant_cutovers.py`.
A curated JSON rather than an `sp500_tickers` column: that table is rebuilt from
Wikipedia, so a roster refresh would silently overwrite hand-established evidence. And
Wikipedia can itself be wrong in this exact way -- it had already moved XOM to the holdco.

BOUNDARY HAND-ADJUDICATED 2026-09-10 to 2022-05-10, the successor's first 10-Q, and NOT the 2023-08-08 the automatic rule proposed. ⚠ APO is the one register entry where both registrants filed a FULL quarterly consolidating series in parallel -- AAM 2022-05 .. 2023-08 at a 91-day median cadence alongside the new parent's own 92-day series -- so the generic 'day after the predecessor's last filing' rule would have kept AAM's 2022-2023 SUBSIDIARY accounts and excluded the parent's for five quarters, which is the blend the dated split exists to prevent. Oracle 4 fixes the date independently: the successor's first 10-K restates AAM's FY2021 as its comparative column (8 of 8 annual facts agree), so FY2022 is the first period the parent owns and the seam falls at Q1 2022. Contrast LIN and VTRS, where the successor's pre-boundary filings are SPARSE (3 filings over 12 months, and Upjohn carve-out reports respectively) and are correctly excluded instead.
